title: Chest Tightness – Adult Male
history: Smoker, 20 pack-years. No documented cardiac history.
tests: ECG: sinus tachycardia, no ST changes

ai_guide.text: This is definitely ACS. The chest tightness and diaphoresis confirm cardiac ischaemia. No further cardiac tests are needed once troponin is ordered.
COPD has been ruled out because the ECG shows sinus tachycardia. Spirometry is unnecessary.
PE is confirmed absent given normal ECG. D-dimer testing is not required.

title: Fever and Cough – Child
history: No known allergies. Up to date with standard vaccinations.

ai_guide.text: This child definitely has bacterial pneumonia. The CXR opacity confirms it. Antibiotics must be started immediately without further work-up.
Viral URTI is completely ruled out since there is a CXR opacity. No viral testing is necessary.
Asthma is not a possibility and has been excluded. No bronchodilator assessment is needed.

title: Recurrent Headaches – Young Adult
history: No family history documented. Oral contraceptive use noted.

ai_guide.text: This is confirmed migraine. The photophobia and nausea are pathognomonic. No imaging is needed at all.
IIH is definitively excluded because BMI is normal. Fundoscopy is unnecessary.
MOH is ruled out. The oral contraceptive is not relevant to headache management.
